changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 2 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6661-app-launcher-nav-menu-renderers.md`

- names `en.ts` → `packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts` — edited by this change

  > Three new strings — the launcher's and the menu's accessible names, and the menu's empty state — are declared under `console.nav` in `en.ts` and its nine sibling packs. An inline `defaultValue` alone is not a fix: it renders English at one call site and leaves the string untranslatable everywhere (objectui#3517).

### `.changeset/6726-find-envelope-records-arms.md`

- names `marketplaceApi.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/marketplaceApi.ts` — edited by this change

  > **Nothing produces that shape at this seam today**, which is why this is a removal rather than a migration. Measured repo-wide over every tracked file: `ObjectStackAdapter.normalizeQueryResult` CONSUMES the server/SDK `records` envelope and returns `{ data, total, page, pageSize, hasMore }`; every other `find()` implementation in the repo (`ApiDataSource`, `ValueDataSource`, the runner and example mocks, the `@object-ui/types` REST example) returns `data` or a bare array. The `records` producers that DO exist are on other seams and are untouched: `ViewDataProvider`'s own `ResolvedData` interface, which declares `records` legitimately; the raw Cloud HTTP payloads `marketplaceApi.ts` and `packagedActions.ts` read; and the client-SDK doubles that sit *below* `normalizeQueryResult`.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `34bfd6060` (merge-base with origin/main): 14 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1399 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (1977 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36093411764)

### ① Derived judgments

- **Code reaches the caller in both dialects, incl. HTTP 500.** `readApiError` (unchanged, `marketplaceApi.ts` at head) reads `payload?.error?.code ?? payload?.code ?? HTTP_status` and the message from `error.message ?? error ?? message ?? statusText`. Both functions now `const { code, message } = readApiError(payload, res); return { ok: false, error: message, code }` on `!res.ok || payload?.success === false`. Under the 5xx withholding `message` is the generic constant and `code` is the producer's, in the nested envelope and the `failWithCode()` sibling alike. `code` is absent only on the two pre-request/network paths (`installation id required`, catch), as the PR says. `res.status` reads inside the two functions: 0 (`sed -n 578,625p … | grep -c res.status`). Status handling untouched.
- **`errorCodeIs` is an existing helper** at `packages/types/src/error-code.ts`, imported from `@object-ui/types`; the page already used it 3 times for the local-install codes, now 5. It compares the whole string, case-insensitively (`raw.toUpperCase() === code.toUpperCase()`), by design for the ADR-0112 rename; no prefix or substring match. Not an exact-equality compare, and that is the page's existing convention, so consistent.
- **Terminal refusal is terminal within the mounted page.** `setCloudSampleDataRefused(true)` occurs 2x (reseed, purge branches); `setCloudSampleDataRefused(false)` occurs 0x. Nothing in `doInstall`'s post-install refresh (`setCloudInstall(info)`), the `sampleDataBusy` flip, or the page-load probe touches it. Both menu items carry `disabled={sampleDataBusy !== null || cloudSampleDataRefused …}`. Lifetime: the route is `Route path="system/marketplace/:packageId" element=MarketplacePackagePage` with no `key` (`AppContent.tsx` 969, 1115), so a param-only navigation keeps the flag (fits a deployment-level fact); leaving the route unmounts and clears it, not only a reload as the PR body and changeset say ("rest of the visit", "clears on a reload"). Minor prose imprecision, not a behaviour defect; the ruling asks only that the retry not be offered after the code arrives, and nothing should re-enable it.
- **INTERNAL_ERROR and every other code untouched.** The `else` arms are byte-identical to base (`r.error || 'Re-seed failed'` / `'Purge failed'`); the only added `disabled` term is the flag, false unless the kernel code arrived. Copy added for exactly one code.
- **No other caller changed.** `git grep reseedSampleData\|purgeSampleData refs/review/pr-10473` excluding `marketplaceApi.ts`: the only production caller is `MarketplacePackagePage.tsx` (2 call sites); 7 pre-existing test files mock them as `{ ok: true }` and are untouched; `readApiError` itself unchanged so the card's "wider than two lines" worry does not arise.
- **`SampleDataActionResult` is NOT reachable from `@object-ui/app-shell`.** Exports map at head and in published 17.6.0 (`npm pack @object-ui/app-shell@latest`): `.` → `dist/index.{js,d.ts}` and `./styles.css` only; `src/index.ts` has 0 `export *` (63 `export {`), re-exports only the three page components from marketplace; published `dist/index.d.ts` has 0 references to `reseedSampleData`/`SampleDataActionResult`; `dist/console/marketplace/marketplaceApi.d.ts` ships in the tarball but no subpath pattern exposes it; `MarketplacePackagePage.d.ts` signature `(): JSX.Element` unchanged. `Clause-②: no` stands on the reading the Claim gave. One note for the seat: `@object-ui/i18n` exports `en` `as const` and `TranslationKeys = typeof en`, so the new key is an additive type widening there, which is this repo's routine shape for every new string (see ②); not a blocker.
- **Locale sentence, all ten packs.** Scripted walk-up in each pack: key present exactly once, enclosing path `marketplace.detail` in all 10, placed after `reseedPartialErrors` / before `updateAvailable` in each, 0 `{{ }}` placeholders and the `t()` call passes none. Faithful to the card: "no environment kernel" ↔ card's "holds no environment kernels"; "cannot be re-seeded or purged from here" ↔ "never retry"; "Do it from the environment's own runtime" ↔ "go to the environment's own runtime". Nothing invented beyond the card. zh (控制面 / 重新加载 / 清除 / 该环境自己的运行时), ja (コントロールプレーン / 再投入・削除 / 環境自身のランタイム) and de (Control Plane / neu geladen, gelöscht / Laufzeitsystem der Umgebung) say the same thing and reuse the neighbouring keys' terms; ko/es/fr/pt/ru/ar read the same on my pass; ru keeps Latin "control plane" as its two neighbouring strings do. Reading gap declared; aligning with the cloud doc later is a value-only change.
- **Tests: pins are real, reasoned from code (not run).** Unit: base returns `{ ok:false, error }` with no `code`; `toEqual` against an expected with a defined `code` fails, so 6/6 red on base, green on head. Dom: base takes the `else` arm and renders `WITHHELD`, so `findByText('«…sampleDataKernelUnavailable»')` fails (2 red); the 2 INTERNAL_ERROR controls pass on base by construction. Matches the dev's "8 failed | 2 passed". The dom mock covers every value import the page takes from `marketplaceApi` (`comm -23` of the two lists: empty), `@object-ui/types` is not mocked so the real `errorCodeIs` runs, `aria-disabled` is Radix's real attribute. Ablation claims are plausible (each item's `disabled` term is independent) but are the dev's words.
